extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys and agents) preparing or defending AIA trial proceedings before the PTAB
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards for initiating, prosecuting, defending, and managing AIA trial proceedings before the PTAB (IPR, PGR, CBM, and derivation). Covers petition drafting, institution standards, claim construction, discovery, evidence, estoppel, joinder, and related timing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard — IPR
rubrics_metrics.description: IPR: “a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail” with respect to at least one challenged claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the threshold the Board uses to decide whether to institute an IPR. The petition should show a reasonable likelihood of prevailing on at least one claim challenged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard — PGR/CBM
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM/PGR: “more likely than not that at least one claim is unpatentable” or the petition raises “a novel or unsettled legal question that is important to other patents or applications.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PGR/CBM institution requires a higher likelihood standard than IPR — more likely than not — or that the petition presents an important novel legal question. Draft petitions to meet this higher threshold for PGR/CBM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of grounds in petition — IPR
rubrics_metrics.description: IPR: only on § 102 and § 103 grounds, and only on basis of prior art consisting of patents and printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR petitions must be limited to anticipation and obviousness based on patents and printed publications; other invalidity grounds are unavailable in IPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of grounds in petition — PGR
rubrics_metrics.description: PGR: on any grounds for invalidity (except best mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-grant review permits challenging patents on essentially any invalidity ground other than best mode; petitions should be drafted to encompass the broader array of substantive grounds where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered Business Method (CBM) scope
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM: same as PGR, but must be a 'covered business method' patent — claims a method or corresponding apparatus for performing data processing or other operations used in the practice, administration, or management of a financial product or service — and does not include patents for 'technological inventions'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM petitions must assert the patent is a covered business method. A technological invention is excluded: whether claimed subject matter as a whole recites a technological feature that is novel and unobvious over prior art, and solves a technical problem using a technical solution. Emphasize financial-product nexus and absence of technological invention when filing CBM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and civil-action bar
rubrics_metrics.description: Review is barred if petitioner or RPI filed a 'civil action' challenging validity of a claim of the patent (DJ action) before filing petition. IPR is barred if petition is filed more than 1 year after date a complaint alleging infringement is served. If petitioner or RPI files a 'civil action' challenging validity on or after filing date of IPR petition, civil action is automatically stayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for prior or concurrent civil actions and the one-year statutory window (35 U.S.C. § 315(b)). Be aware that counterclaims are not 'civil actions' for this purpose. Timeliness and prior litigation status are dispositive and should be evaluated early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Estoppel for civil actions and ITC proceedings precludes petitioner, any real party in interest, or privy from later challenging the same patent claim. IPR/PGR: any ground 'raised or reasonably could have raised' during review that resulted in final written decision. CBM: any ground 'raised' during review that resulted in final written decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the broader IPR/PGR estoppel (including grounds that reasonably could have been raised) versus CBM's narrower estoppel. Craft petitions and settlement strategies with estoppel consequences in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof and timing for final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard of proof: a 'preponderance of evidence' (lower than 'clear and convincing'). Final decision within 12 months of institution (can extend by 6 months, but only for 'good cause').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect adjudication under the preponderance standard and plan for the statutory timelines; extensions are rare and require showing good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions — compliance requirements (page limits, exhibits, notices, related proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumventing page limit: 37 C.F.R. § 42.6; Exhibit labeling and numbering: § 42.63; Mandatory notices: § 42.8 — include in petition; count toward page limit. Related proceedings: § 42.8(b)(2) ('any other judicial or administrative matter that would affect, or be affected by, a decision in the proceeding.'). Claim construction required: § 42.104(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply strictly with Part 42 formatting and notice rules. Mandatory notices count toward page limits; observe exhibit labeling/numbering rules and disclosure of related proceedings to avoid procedural defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition drafting strategy — scope and depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Better to provide detailed analysis for limited number of challenges, rather than identify large number of challenges for which little analysis is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on a smaller set of well-developed grounds with sound, claim-by-claim legal analysis and pinpoint citations to the evidentiary record rather than numerous thinly-supported grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and citation standards in petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Support conclusions with: sound, complete legal analysis per claim per ground; pinpoint citations to evidentiary record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every legal assertion should be tied to record evidence and explained claim-by-claim. Avoid sweeping assertions without specific citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard (BRI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard: broadest reasonable interpretation (BRI) in light of the specification of the patent in which claim appears. The Board will construe claim terms even if the parties do not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed constructions should be justified with evidence; most cases require more construction than a mere restatement of the BRI standard. Anticipate the Board performing constructions and prepare supporting evidence and arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim charts — purpose and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose of claim charts is to summarize the evidence, not the argument. Claim charts support narrative analysis; they do not replace it. Use two-column format. Provide pinpoint references to the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use claim charts as a concise evidence map that directly supports the narrative analysis; do not rely on charts alone. Follow two-column format and ensure precise citations to exhibits and record locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert declarations — content and weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide underlying objective facts to support testimony; unsupported testimony is entitled to little or no weight (37 C.F.R. 42.65(a); see IPR2013-00022, Paper 43 denying petition). Avoid merely 'expertizing' claim charts and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft declarations to add objective factual support (e.g., experiments, data, methodology) rather than conclusory expert opinions reciting argument already in claim charts; focus on demonstrative tutorials where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness challenges — required analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the Graham factors. Explain the rationale to combine. Support the rationale to combine with evidence. Differentiate multiple grounds to avoid redundancy denials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform a full Graham-factor analysis and provide concrete factual support for any rationale to combine references; ensure each ground is distinct to avoid the Board denying redundant grounds (see CBM2012-00003).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner preliminary response strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability is not decided at institution stage. Focus arguments on dispositive issues: standing (statutory bar, RPI/privy issues); reference is not prior art; prior art lacks a material limitation or teaches away; unreasonable claim construction. Arguments not raised in preliminary response are not waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the preliminary response to address jurisdictional and threshold deficiencies and to show why the petition fails on dispositive grounds; preserve other arguments for later stages (they are not waived if omitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery framework and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery — 37 CFR §§ 42.51-53: Mandatory initial disclosures; with parties' agreement file agreement with Board before filing of patent owner preliminary response & may automatically take discovery upon institution of trial. Without agreement – seek discovery by motion. Routine discovery: documents cited; cross-examination for submitted testimony; and information inconsistent with positions advanced. Additional discovery standard: 'in the interest of justice' for IPR, whereas the lower good cause is used for PGR and CBM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely serve mandatory disclosures and, if possible, agree to discovery terms. For additional discovery, expect the Board to apply differing standards (stricter 'interest of justice' for IPR). Be specific in requests—documents that are specific and relevant are more likely to be granted than broad/general requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional discovery five-factor test
rubrics_metrics.description: Five-factor test articulated in IPR2012-00001 (Garmin v. Cuozzo): (1) More than a possibility and mere allegation? (2) Seeking opponent's litigation position early? (3) Ability to generate by other means? (4) Instructions clear? (5) Overly burdensome to answer?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame discovery requests to satisfy these factors: show particularized need, avoid fishing for litigation positions, demonstrate the evidence can't be obtained by other means, make requests clear, and limit burdensomeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions and testimony procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Rules of Evidence apply. Objections to admissibility waived. Follow the Testimony Guidelines (Practice Guide Appendix D): No 'speaking' objections or coaching; Instructions not to answer are limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare witnesses and counsel to follow the Board's testimony rules; avoid objections that the Board deems waived and avoid coaching witnesses during depositions. Follow Appendix D guidance closely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Joinder: Must be a like review proceeding. Requires filing a motion and petition. File within one month of institution. Impact on schedule important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seeking to join an existing proceeding, ensure the new petition is of the same type and file the joinder motion/petition promptly (within one month) and account for any schedule consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation proceeding requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Derivation: Only an applicant for patent may file a petition to institute a derivation proceeding. Applicant must file petition within 1 year of the date of the first publication of a claim to an invention that is the same or substantially the same as the earlier application's claim to the invention. The petition must set forth with particularity the basis for finding that an inventor named in an earlier application or patent derived the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivation petitions have strict standing and timeliness rules and require a particularized factual pleading showing derivation; prepare documentary and other evidence to meet the particularity requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional CBM special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitional CBM generally employs PGR procedures/standards except: petitioner, RPI, or privy must have been sued for infringement or charged with infringement; can file any time after issuance (not just within 9 months); both pre-AIA and post-AIA patents are eligible; ground cannot be based on 35 U.S.C. § 102(e) secret prior art; civil action/ITC estoppel: any ground 'raised'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For transitional CBM petitions, demonstrate the required litigation nexus and be mindful of the special eligibility and estoppel rules (and the §102(e) secret prior art limitation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction required in petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim construction required: § 42.104(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must include proposed claim constructions as required by the rule; failure to provide constructions risks procedural or substantive weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner identity and effect of filing a civil action after petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner = any third party (not patent owner). If petitioner or RPI files a 'civil action' challenging validity on or after filing date of IPR petition, civil action is automatically stayed. A counter-claim challenging validity is not a 'civil action' for purposes of the civil-action bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand who qualifies as a petitioner and how subsequent district-court filings interact with the IPR (stay). Use this to strategize litigation timing and forum selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical drafting tip — target limited, supported challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Better to provide detailed analysis for limited number of challenges, rather than identify large number of challenges for which little analysis is provided. Claim charts and expert declarations should support, not substitute for, narrative legal analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize depth over breadth: develop claim-specific narratives, supported by properly prepared charts, declarations, and pinpoint citations to record evidence.
